_readme: Hand-verified real-MLB jersey/team stints for spans data/processed/player_seasons.json + draft_picks.json/keepers.json can't produce an accurate jersey badge for on their own. Two distinct reasons an entry exists here, and an entry can be either or both: (1) ESPN's API reports no jersey numbers at all before 2017 (data/README.md 318) -- a structural gap covering ~780 players / ~2,400 player-seasons league-wide; (2) a player was traded mid-season, so the single pro_team_id draft_picks.json/keepers.json carry for that year (by this project's one-value-per-year convention, data/manual/pro-team-overrides.json) shows only one of the two teams he actually wore a jersey for that year -- these years need two adjacent entries, both with the same startYear/endYear, one per team. This file is NOT pipeline output: it's read directly by the app (app/scripts/sync-data.mjs copies it straight to public/data/, same as retired-owners.json) and merged into app/src/lib/playerPositions.ts's getJerseyHistory picture without touching player_seasons.json or draft_picks.json, so scripts/validate.py's check_player_positions early-jersey invariant stays intact and the draft-picks single-value convention is undisturbed for every other purpose (draft board, keeper math, etc). Each entry covers a [start_year, end_year] span (inclusive) for one team/one number and REPLACES whatever getJerseyHistory would otherwise derive for every year in that span -- a single full-season team stint that ESPN's own per-year data already covers correctly (single team, known jersey) does NOT need an entry here, only spans ESPN can't represent alone. `start_date`/`end_date` (real calendar dates, ISO YYYY-MM-DD) are optional and come from the MLB Stats API's per-player transaction log (person endpoint, hydrate=transactions, via the mlb-stats MCP server) -- include them when known; omit start_date on a player's earliest tracked stint or end_date on one that bridges forward into ESPN's own later per-year data (getJerseyHistory only needs the true start of a run and the true end, and picks up whichever boundary a later segment in the same run supplies). pro_team_id values are cross-checked against this project's own draft_picks.json/keepers.json for the years they cover. This is a large backlog (both kinds of gap, across many more players than covered so far) being filled in incrementally across sessions. To find backfill gaps: any (player_id, year) in player_seasons.json with jersey=null where draft_picks.json/keepers.json resolves a non-zero pro_team_id and no entry below covers it. To find trade-split gaps: any player who changed real MLB teams mid-season -- no systematic list exists in this project's own data before transactions.json's 2019+ coverage, so this has to be checked player by player via the transactions hydrate above; a good place to start is every player already in data/manual/pro-team-overrides.json, since a free-agency-lag bug there means that player's team history is already known to need close reading. To find a third kind of gap -- a year with NO draft_picks.json/keepers.json record at all (so proTeamIdByYear has nothing to resolve, and no badge shows), but which DOES have a player_seasons.json row for that year (meaning the player really was on a fantasy roster that season, just via an in-season waiver pickup rather than a draft/keeper pick): these are NOT permanently unfixable the way they look -- an override entry here works standalone regardless of draft_picks.json, so real-world team/jersey knowledge can restore the badge (see the Albert Pujols 2021 entry below: no draft record existed for that mid-season Angels release/Dodgers signing, but the season row did, so it got two manual stints anyway). Confirmed to affect ~30 more player-years across players already covered in this file as of the 2026-07-27 audit (e.g. Kershaw 2024-2025, Trout 2011-2012, McCutchen 2009/2025, Votto 2021/2023, Cabrera 2021-2022, Longoria 2020-2022) -- these are known but not yet fixed; check `sorted(y for y in player_seasons_years if y not in draft_or_keeper_years)` per player_id to find them for any player, not just new ones.
